A-10 Event capacity adjustment

Bangla name: ইভেন্ট ধারণক্ষমতা সমন্বয়

← 10 · Admin portal · Contents · Open queries

1. Name and purpose

Capacity adjustment. The number of seats that customers can buy online at a level is TicketingCapacity in Booking. An admin changes it by allocating seats (adds capacity, optionally naming exact seats) or deallocating seats (takes back part of an earlier allocation). Every adjustment is recorded with a number and the admin who made it. Concepts: Redis live capacity, distributed locks, queue-driven processing.

2. Trigger and actor

Staff on the event's Gallery Update tab (/events/event-details/:id), columns "Remaining Allocated" and "De-allocated". The server has no authorization on this controller (EventCapacityAdjustmentController has no [Authorize]; a comment in the manager says "TODO: add check for admin role").

3. Business flow

  1. Choose a level, press Add under Allocated, enter the number of seats (or a percentage of the level, or the exact seat labels for a seated level) and save.
  2. To take seats back, open the allocation list, pick an earlier allocation, and deallocate part of it.
  3. The adjustment appears in the history, and the event's online-ticket total changes.

4. Technical flow

  1. [HTTP + user token] The tab lists adjustments with GET /booking/api/v1/event-capacity-adjustment/by-event-level?eventId&levelId&action&programId (the Booking service, called directly by the portal).
  2. [HTTP + user token] Save: POST /booking/api/v1/event-capacity-adjustment with EventCapacityAdjustment {eventId, galleryId, blockId, levelId, ticketingCapacity, hasSeats, seats, action, caId}. EventCapacityAdjustmentManager.CreateAsync: - validate: ids greater than 0; ticketingCapacity > 0; the gallery, block and level of the event must be active (gallery_or_block_or_level_inactive) and the ids must belong together (unauthorized_access); for Deallocate a caId is required, the earlier allocation must exist ("Selected Adjustment is not found."), the amount must not exceed it ("Ticketing capacity must be less than allocated seats."), must not exceed the live capacity (no_seats_available), and the sum of all deallocations of that allocation must not exceed it (cannot_deallocate_more_than_allocate); with seats: deallocated seats must all be available ("Unavailable seats: ...") and allocated seats must not already exist ("Cannot allocate these seats because they already exist in the system: ..."); - take the lock level_booking_{event}_{gallery}_{block}_{level} (expiry 30 s, wait 15 s, retry 1 s) (X-25); - CapacityManager.BookLevelCapacity(... isIncrease = (action == Allocate), orderType = Admin, capacityAction = Allocation): for an admin order it changes the Redis capacity hash field level_live:{...} at once (increment or decrement) and updates the live seat list, then publishes [SQS: OrderSuccess] to update the database capacity (S-01) and [SQS: EventCapacity] to update the event total (S-02); - insert the adjustment row (PublicId, AdjustmentNumber = unique code, CreatedBy = the admin's id, ProgramId); - delete event_total_online_ticket:{eventId} from Redis.
  3. If the lock is not obtained in 15 s: "Failed to acquire lock to update level capacity."

7. Data and side effects

EventCapacityAdjustments row; Redis live capacity changed at once; two queue messages; the database capacity changes when the worker runs; activity log (X-24).

9. Handover notes

  1. No authorization. Anyone who can reach the Booking service path can allocate or deallocate capacity of any event; the manager records CreatedBy from the token's user id (User.GetId()), and the controller does not stop a call without a token (what GetId() returns then is not checked here) (X-18).
  2. Redis first, database later. The live count changes immediately; the database TicketingCapacity follows within the worker cycle (up to about 30 seconds per batch). A deallocation validated against the live capacity can pass while the database still shows the old number (S-01 notes 1 and 2).
  3. The adjustment row is written after the capacity change. If the insert fails, the capacity has changed (live and queued) but no history row exists.
  4. No published or time check. An adjustment can be made at any time, including during sales and after the event started.
  5. Allocate may exceed the level's seating capacity. The validation compares only with live capacity for deallocation; for allocation there is no upper bound against SeatingCapacity.
  6. The 15-second lock wait is shared with customers booking the same level, so heavy booking on a level can delay an admin adjustment.
